This reminds me a bit of my proposal for municipal broadband as an alternative to 'net neutrality'. A big part of the problem with e.g., Comcast is again authoritarianism. They have contracts with various municipalities granting them a government-protected monopoly. The excuse given is that they don't want backhoes and trenching equipment digging up all of the neighborhoods every time a new player enters the market.

My proposal, then, is to let the municipality "own" the conduit running between all the buildings. Essentially, I trust them far enough to manage a small hole in the ground-- provided they keep the conduit wide enough for at least three competitors to run e.g., fiber through. Market competitors then, would bid on access to the conduit on maybe an annual basis. They'd also manage the fiber and terminal equipment like routers, etc. however they saw fit.
